detailed_rationale:
Aadhar Housing Finance is a focused affordable-housing NBFC (home loans 73%, loan-against-property 27%, fully secured and retail) that crossed the Rs 30,000 cr AUM milestone in FY26, growing AUM 20% YoY to Rs 30,571 cr with over 336,000 loan accounts. As a housing-finance NBFC, the sector D/E exemption applies (D/E 2.49 reflects normal on-lending leverage, not distress); the more relevant quality signals -- asset quality and returns -- are both strong: gross NPA stands at 1.08%, having improved 30 bps sequentially, and the company posted a 4.4% return on assets and 15.9% return on equity for FY26, both healthy for a housing financier.

Growth has been broad-based and accelerating into the year-end: FY26 PAT grew 22% to Rs 1,108 cr, Q4 PAT alone grew 27% YoY to Rs 311 cr, and Q4 disbursements of Rs 3,087 cr (+20% YoY) were the highest quarterly disbursement figure in the company's history -- evidence that growth is being driven by continued origination momentum rather than one-off items. Management has set an explicit target of Rs 50,000 cr AUM by FY29, which implies a forward AUM CAGR of roughly 19-20% from the current base -- a useful, company-provided anchor for a forward growth view rather than simply extrapolating the trailing print.

At a PE of ~20x for an HFC with pristine and improving asset quality, a 4.4% ROA, and a credible, well-articulated growth target, the valuation looks reasonable rather than stretched. Affordable housing finance in India remains a large, structurally underpenetrated market, and Aadhar's fully secured, retail-only book reduces the credit-risk profile relative to unsecured-lending NBFCs.
recommendation_rationale: Already a quant-Hold; the strong, well-evidenced growth and improving asset quality are genuine positives, but nothing here rises to a case for treating this as needing escalation or a harsher call -- this is a clean, well-run compounder trading at a fair multiple for its own guided growth rate.
summary: Aadhar Housing Finance is a fast-growing, fully secured affordable-housing lender that just crossed Rs 30,000 crore in loans under management, with improving asset quality and healthy returns. Management has laid out a credible path to nearly double loans under management by FY29. We rate this a Hold: fundamentals are genuinely strong, and the valuation looks fair for the growth on offer, without an obvious mispricing in either direction.
positive_para: Fully secured, retail-only loan book (home loans + loan against property) growing AUM 20% YoY with pristine and improving asset quality (GNPA 1.08%, improving 30 bps sequentially) and a strong 4.4% ROA. Record quarterly disbursements (Rs 3,087 cr in Q4) show origination momentum is broad-based, and management has articulated a credible, specific growth target (Rs 50,000 cr AUM by FY29) that roughly matches the current growth trajectory.
negative_para: As with any housing financier, a sharp deterioration in the broader real-estate or employment-income environment would pressure both origination volumes and collections, and affordable-housing borrowers (often informal-income) are somewhat more exposed to income-shock risk than prime-housing borrowers, even though current asset quality shows no sign of this.
reverse_dcf_judgment: At ~20x earnings for an HFC guiding to ~19-20% AUM growth with a 4.4% ROA and improving asset quality, the valuation is a close, honest match to the company's own growth target -- fair value, not an obvious bargain nor overpriced.
